key_insight: A continuous-time rate certificate can be transferred to a discrete contact-splitting optimizer when the flow admits a contact Hamiltonian structure and the splitting meets explicit backward-error and shadowing conditions.
engineering_relevance: This gives optimization engineers a principled way to design and analyze split-step solvers with provable geometric decay behavior, especially for accelerated and damped methods.
method: Define a contact Hamiltonian with an augmented energy certificate and conformal decay rate.
Use an order-r contact splitting plus backward error analysis to track a modified Hamiltonian over a finite horizon.
Verify transfer through three checkable hypotheses, with special corollaries for heavy-ball and state-dependent damping.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical experiments on ill-conditioned benchmarks and deep-learning tasks, showing predicted conformal-factor tracking orders and competitive performance.
watch_item: The guarantee is finite-horizon and depends on specific structural hypotheses, so performance may degrade if the problem lacks a valid contact Hamiltonian certificate or if step size is too large.
paper_title: When Rates Are Geometric: Rate-Certificate Transfer for Contact Splittings in Optimization
